To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Tc‐99 m methylene diphosphate (MDP) is an effective renal scintigraphic agent for the determination of differential renal function.

1) The early characteristics of renal Tc-MDP handling are sufficiently similar to Tc-DTPAs and Tc-GHAs so that accurate estimates are possible of differential renal function with this agent; 2) Tc-MDP‐determined renal differential most probably reflects differential glomeru­lar filtration rate; and 3) The use of Tc-MPD for this purpose is a valid alternative to Tc-DPTA and Tc-99-GHA.
Tc‐99M MDP is a useful agent for quantitative assessment of relative renal function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of bone imaging agents for quantitative assessment of differential renal function.
the development of a novel method of determining the differential renal function of the kidneys in vivo.
the development of new methods for the quantification and evaluation of renal function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Tc‐99 m MDP is an excellent agent for the determination of differential renal function.
Tc-99 m MDP can be utilized to quantitate renal function in a manner similar to that for other radiotracers.
Tc-99M MDP is a useful renal imaging agent, and that it is a useful renal function agent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MDP is a good tracer for differential renal function, and that it can be used for that purpose in patients who have had a previous Tc-99M pyrophosphate bone scan.

the early characteristics (1–3 min) of renal handling of 99mTc-MDP are sufficient similar to those of 99m Tc-DTP and 99m T-c-GHA, that accurate estimates of relative renal function can be obtained with this agent.

the early characteristics (i.e., the first 5 minutes after injection) of the renal handling of TCMDP are sufficiently similar (in terms of renal differential function) to those of TCDTPA and TCGHA, so that accurate estimates are possible with this tracer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bone tracer, Tc-MDP, can be used for quantitation of differential renal function.
Tc-99 MDP can be used to quantify differential function in the kidneys.
Tc-99M MDP can be used to determine relative renal function.
